L9-PDF1-p1.text:
108 Finger Permutations - Level 9
Mid-Pattern Position Transfer: 2+2 In-Code Shift Control
Level 8 shifted between complete four-note cells. Level 9 moves the boundary inside the code, after note 2, while the pick stays on one string.
1. Keep both frames exact
P5: 1=5, 2=6, 3=7, 4=8.
P7: 1=7, 2=8, 3=9, 4=10.
Use the assigned finger in each frame.
Do not stretch from the old position.
2. Split every code 2+2
Notes 1-2: starting position.
Release after note 2.
Notes 3-4: destination position.
The digit order never changes.
3. Shift the frame, not the pitch
Move hand and thumb as one unit.
The next note may rise, repeat, or fall.
Land with no slide, scrape, or delay.
Keep the unused strings silent.
Worked example - code 1234
The center divider is the shift boundary. Repeat the one-string template on each string in the printed route.
SHIFT UP - E > A > D > G > B > e
P5
P7
S|5-6------|9-10-----|
SHIFT DOWN - e > B > G > D > A > E
P7
P5
S|7-8------|7-8------|
PASS 1
Play notes 1-2, stop, release pressure, move the hand frame, then play notes 3-4.
Use the stop only to verify a clean release and exact landing; do not drag a finger along the string.
PASS 2
Remove the stop. Play straight eighths, lightly accent note 3, then remove the accent and convert to 16ths.
Use D-U | D-U and U-D | U-D so note 3 begins with the same pick direction as note 1.
Important: on the downward 1234 form, the tab repeats frets 7-8, but the hand still changes from P7 fingers 1-2 to P5 fingers 3-4.
Practice protocol
1
Choose one 12-exercise set.
2
Begin 8-12 BPM below your clean
Level 8 continuous tempo.
3
Run SHIFT UP and SHIFT DOWN
with a downstroke start.
4
Repeat both routes with an
upstroke start.
5
After three clean loops, add
2 BPM at the next session.
6
After two missed landings, slides,
or tension, reduce 4-6 BPM.
Advance after the full set is clean both ways on two separate days.
Standard tuning. P5 = frets 5-8; P7 = frets 7-10. Shift the whole hand frame after note 2.

L9-TXT1-1-25.text:
108 FINGER PERMUTATIONS - LEVEL 9: MID-PATTERN POSITION TRANSFER
2+2 in-code shifts on one string at a time in standard tuning.
P5 mapping: 1=index/fret 5, 2=middle/fret 6, 3=ring/fret 7, 4=pinky/fret 8.
P7 mapping: 1=index/fret 7, 2=middle/fret 8, 3=ring/fret 9, 4=pinky/fret 10.

MOVEMENT RULE
SHIFT UP: play digits 1-2 of the code in P5, release pressure, shift the whole hand frame two frets,
then play digits 3-4 in P7. Repeat on E-A-D-G-B-e, one string at a time.
SHIFT DOWN: play digits 1-2 in P7, shift the whole hand frame down two frets, then play digits 3-4 in P5.
Repeat on e-B-G-D-A-E, one string at a time. The center divider marks the shift after note 2.
The position direction describes the hand frame, not the melodic interval; the next note may rise, repeat, or fall.
Even when the fret numbers overlap, relocate the frame and use the assigned finger rather than stretching.

WHY THIS IS LEVEL 9
Level 8 placed the shift between complete four-note codes. Level 9 moves the shift inside each code while keeping
the picking hand on one string. This isolates release timing, target-finger preparation, thumb movement, and
reconstruction of the four-fret frame without adding string-crossing difficulty.

PRACTICE RULE
Use one 12-exercise set per session and begin 8-12 BPM below your clean Level 8 continuous tempo.
Pass 1: play notes 1-2, stop, release, relocate, and play notes 3-4. Do not slide along the string.
Pass 2: remove the stop, play straight eighths, lightly accent note 3, remove the accent, then convert to 16ths.
Play both routes with a downstroke start and then an upstroke start: D-U | D-U and U-D | U-D.
After three clean loops, add 2 BPM next session. After two missed landings, slides, or rising tension, reduce 4-6 BPM.
Advance after the full set is clean in both directions on two separate days.
